power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

text.text: For seventy years, minds and machines have been studied by comparison: can machines model, imitate or outperform us?

In bounded domains this comparison has saturated, and machines now produce certified knowledge that no person can inspect; a complete Lean formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem runs to 13.5 million lines.
We argue that the object of study must move from the performance gap to the change in minds that learn from machines.
We propose Reverse Cognition: a search for faithful, explicitly limited representations through which a person can acquire a certified structure and keep it once the machine is withdrawn.
In the public formalization, only 5.7% of the theorems beneath the four steps of the human proof belong to a single step.

We define audit criteria for representational routes, machine operations that could make such objects followable, predictions that separate appropriation from offloading, and a study sequence to test them.
Since Turing asked whether a machine could pass for a person 1 , the relation between minds and machines has largely been studied as a comparison.
text.formatted: Since Turing asked whether a machine could pass for a person <ref type="bibr" target="#b0">1</ref> , the relation between minds and machines has largely been studied as a comparison.

text.text: Can a model imitate human language, vision or reasoning?
Does it match people on a benchmark?
Does a human-AI pair outperform either member?
These programmes remain valuable.
Turing-style tests show a narrowing gap between human and machine outputs 2 , and a meta-analysis of 106 experiments found that human-AI teams do not, on average, outperform their better member 3.
text.formatted: Turing-style tests show a narrowing gap between human and machine outputs <ref type="bibr" target="#b1">2</ref> , and a meta-analysis of 106 experiments found that human-AI teams do not, on average, outperform their better member <ref type="bibr" target="#b2">3</ref>.

text.text: A neighbouring programme treats machines themselves as objects of behavioural science 4 , building models meant to learn and think like people 5 , applying the methods of cognitive psychology to models 6, 7 and even proposing models as stand-ins for human participants 8.
text.formatted: A neighbouring programme treats machines themselves as objects of behavioural science <ref type="bibr" target="#b3">4</ref> , building models meant to learn and think like people <ref type="bibr" target="#b4">5</ref> , applying the methods of cognitive psychology to models <ref type="bibr" target="#b5">6,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b6">7</ref> and even proposing models as stand-ins for human participants <ref type="bibr" target="#b7">8</ref>.

text.text: Even the call for machines that learn and think with people evaluates the partnership mainly by what the pair achieves 9 .
text.formatted: Even the call for machines that learn and think with people evaluates the partnership mainly by what the pair achieves <ref type="bibr" target="#b8">9</ref> .

text.text: In all of these, the experimental gaze rests on the machine or on the joint system.
Comparison is informative when the two terms are close.
It loses information when one term leaves the scale.
Since AlphaGo and AlphaZero 10, 11 , no one asks whether a program plays Go or chess as well as a person; asking would tell us about the program, not the mind.
text.formatted: Since AlphaGo and AlphaZero <ref type="bibr" target="#b9">10,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b10">11</ref> , no one asks whether a program plays Go or chess as well as a person; asking would tell us about the program, not the mind.

text.text: Formal mathematics is joining that list.
In September 2026 a multi-agent AI system completed a machine-checked proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean 12 , following the route of Darmon, Diamond and Taylor 13 .
text.formatted: In September 2026 a multi-agent AI system completed a machine-checked proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean <ref type="bibr" target="#b11">12</ref> , following the route of Darmon, Diamond and Taylor <ref type="bibr" target="#b12">13</ref> .

text.text: This was a formalization of an existing human proof, not an independent discovery 14, 15.
text.formatted: This was a formalization of an existing human proof, not an independent discovery <ref type="bibr" target="#b13">14,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b14">15</ref>.

text.text: We do not claim that comparison was a mistake, nor that cognitive science must be replaced.
We claim that its open variable has moved.
When machines that exceed us in a domain become a main source of its new structure, the scientifically open question is no longer how far the machine's performance is from ours.

It is what happens to human cognition that learns from it: specifically, whether a person, after interacting with machine-built representations, can make reliable inferences without the machine that were previously beyond reach.
This is a claim about human learning, not about machine understanding.
The claim has a long ancestry.

Human minds have always been reshaped by their tools: writing and numerals recycled cortical circuits evolved for other purposes 16 , and cumulative culture transmits cognitive techniques no individual could invent 17 .
text.formatted: Human minds have always been reshaped by their tools: writing and numerals recycled cortical circuits evolved for other purposes <ref type="bibr" target="#b15">16</ref> , and cumulative culture transmits cognitive techniques no individual could invent <ref type="bibr" target="#b16">17</ref> .

text.text: Machines are now becoming participants in that cultural process 18 .
text.formatted: Machines are now becoming participants in that cultural process <ref type="bibr" target="#b17">18</ref> .

text.text: What is new is that some of the structure they transmit has never passed through a human mind, and that its correctness can be certified without one.
A proof is surveyable if a person can take it in and check it.

The computer-assisted proof of the four-colour theorem first raised the possibility of mathematical knowledge that is certain but unsurveyable 19 , its later formal verification removed doubt without restoring surveyability 20 , and the formal proof of the Kepler conjecture extended the case 21.
text.formatted: The computer-assisted proof of the four-colour theorem first raised the possibility of mathematical knowledge that is certain but unsurveyable <ref type="bibr" target="#b18">19</ref> , its later formal verification removed doubt without restoring surveyability <ref type="bibr" target="#b19">20</ref> , and the formal proof of the Kepler conjecture extended the case <ref type="bibr" target="#b20">21</ref>.

text.text: Mathematics is undergoing a broader formal turn 22 , built on proof assistants such as Lean 23.
text.formatted: Mathematics is undergoing a broader formal turn <ref type="bibr" target="#b21">22</ref> , built on proof assistants such as Lean <ref type="bibr" target="#b22">23</ref>.

text.text: The Fermat formalization multiplies it.
Its dependency tree contains 29,511 theorems, supported by about 533,000 further lemmas, in about 13.5 million lines of Lean 12.
text.formatted: Its dependency tree contains 29,511 theorems, supported by about 533,000 further lemmas, in about 13.5 million lines of Lean <ref type="bibr" target="#b11">12</ref>.

text.text: Machines are also producing new mathematics and science, not only checking it: geometry proofs at olympiad level 24 and discoveries across the sciences 25 .
text.formatted: Machines are also producing new mathematics and science, not only checking it: geometry proofs at olympiad level <ref type="bibr" target="#b23">24</ref> and discoveries across the sciences <ref type="bibr" target="#b24">25</ref> .

text.text: The volume of certified or validated machine output is growing faster than any community can read it.
Two distinctions keep this observation honest.
A proof assistant certifies that a statement is derivable from stated premises and rules; it does not show that anyone understands the particular derivation.
Conversely, the impossibility of reading millions of lines does not mean that no one understands the mathematics: the human proof is understood by many experts 14, 15, 26, 27 .
text.formatted: Conversely, the impossibility of reading millions of lines does not mean that no one understands the mathematics: the human proof is understood by many experts <ref type="bibr" target="#b13">14,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b14">15,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b25">26,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b26">27</ref> .

text.text: "Unsurveyed certificate" and "ununderstood mathematics" are different claims.
What is new for psychology is narrower and more useful.
A formally controlled dependency structure fixes truth independently of anyone's comprehension, so understanding becomes a variable that can be measured against an external, checkable standard.
Whether machines themselves understand is debated 28 , but that is not our question.
text.formatted: Whether machines themselves understand is debated <ref type="bibr" target="#b27">28</ref> , but that is not our question.

text.text: AI-supported science may produce illusions of understanding in people 29 ; the surveyability gap makes those illusions testable rather than only arguable.
text.formatted: AI-supported science may produce illusions of understanding in people <ref type="bibr" target="#b28">29</ref> ; the surveyability gap makes those illusions testable rather than only arguable.

text.text: It also gives a reference for a long-standing question in mathematical cognition: what experts do when they read and understand proofs 30-
text.formatted: It also gives a reference for a long-standing question in mathematical cognition: what experts do when they read and understand proofs <ref type="bibr">30-</ref>

text.text: If machines become a main source of new structure, human cognition can move in two directions (Fig. 1).
text.formatted: If machines become a main source of new structure, human cognition can move in two directions (Fig. <ref type="figure" target="#fig_0">1</ref>).

text.text: People acquire new representational coordinates and keep them when the machine is gone.
The evidence is thin but real.
After superhuman Go programs appeared, professional moves became both better and more novel 34 .
text.formatted: After superhuman Go programs appeared, professional moves became both better and more novel <ref type="bibr" target="#b33">34</ref> .

text.text: Four world-class chess players solved more unseen puzzles after studying concepts extracted from AlphaZero's internal representations and filtered for novelty and teachability 35 .
text.formatted: Four world-class chess players solved more unseen puzzles after studying concepts extracted from AlphaZero's internal representations and filtered for novelty and teachability <ref type="bibr" target="#b34">35</ref> .

text.text: Machine learning has pointed expert mathematicians to relations from which new results followed 36 , and AI has been proposed as a potential agent of scientific understanding 37 .
text.formatted: Machine learning has pointed expert mathematicians to relations from which new results followed <ref type="bibr" target="#b35">36</ref> , and AI has been proposed as a potential agent of scientific understanding <ref type="bibr" target="#b36">37</ref> .

text.text: Field and laboratory studies show sizeable productivity gains with generative AI, largest for less experienced workers 38, 39 , and a brief dialogue with a language model reduced conspiracy beliefs durably over two months 40 : machine interaction can change minds in ways that persist.
text.formatted: Field and laboratory studies show sizeable productivity gains with generative AI, largest for less experienced workers <ref type="bibr" target="#b37">38,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b38">39</ref> , and a brief dialogue with a language model reduced conspiracy beliefs durably over two months <ref type="bibr" target="#b39">40</ref> : machine interaction can change minds in ways that persist.

text.text: People hand cognition over and lose it when the machine is gone.
Here the evidence is larger.
In a field experiment with nearly 1,000 students, access to GPT-4 raised practice grades by 48%, but once access ended the same students scored 17% below controls 41 .
text.formatted: In a field experiment with nearly 1,000 students, access to GPT-4 raised practice grades by 48%, but once access ended the same students scored 17% below controls <ref type="bibr" target="#b40">41</ref> .

text.text: AI assistance raises the quality of single ideas while narrowing their diversity 42 ; human-AI feedback loops amplify bias 43 ; jargon raises satisfaction with explanations while lowering comprehension 44 .
text.formatted: AI assistance raises the quality of single ideas while narrowing their diversity <ref type="bibr" target="#b41">42</ref> ; human-AI feedback loops amplify bias <ref type="bibr" target="#b42">43</ref> ; jargon raises satisfaction with explanations while lowering comprehension <ref type="bibr" target="#b43">44</ref> .

text.text: Generative AI raised the rated creativity of individual stories while making stories across writers more similar 45 , and knowledge workers report less critical-thinking effort when they trust AI more 46 .
text.formatted: Generative AI raised the rated creativity of individual stories while making stories across writers more similar <ref type="bibr" target="#b44">45</ref> , and knowledge workers report less critical-thinking effort when they trust AI more <ref type="bibr" target="#b45">46</ref> .

text.text: Both futures are already observed, in different domains and under different conditions.
The question is therefore not whether AI changes minds but which conditions decide the direction.
One contrast in the evidence suggests where to look.
Where minds contracted, the machine supplied answers.
Where they expanded, it supplied structure people had to traverse themselves: positions to play through, concepts to apply, conjectures to prove.
Our working hypothesis is that minds expand when machines supply routes rather than answers.
Navigation offers the right image, provided its history is respected.

Polaris, a convenient northern reference, becomes unusable at southern latitudes; European oceanic navigators had to draw on solar altitude, dead reckoning, unfamiliar stars and improving astronomical technique.
Magellan did not single-handedly reconstruct the southern sky.
The expedition of 1519-1522 generated observations, including those of Andrés de San Martín, and cartographic reconstruction took generations 53.
text.formatted: The expedition of 1519-1522 generated observations, including those of Andrés de San Martín, and cartographic reconstruction took generations <ref type="bibr" target="#b52">53</ref>.

text.text: Later in the sixteenth century, southern star observations by the Dutch navigators Pieter Dirkszoon Keyser and Frederick de Houtman, embedded in the cartographic projects of Petrus Plancius and others, were consolidated into globes, catalogues and eventually the southern plate of Johann Bayer's Uranometria (1603) 54 .

text.text: Local observations were coordinated into a shareable system of positions, patterns and names, built from separate surveys and later reconciled with older records 55 .

text.text: The map was a public reference system for further observation and correction, not an image that guaranteed understanding by itself.
Nor was the southern sky unknown to humanity.
Pacific navigators held sophisticated practices long before European cartography incorporated these stars 56 .
text.formatted: Pacific navigators held sophisticated practices long before European cartography incorporated these stars <ref type="bibr" target="#b55">56</ref> .

text.text: In the Micronesian system analysed by Hutchins, the voyager may hold the canoe conceptually stationary and track the apparent motion of a reference island against star bearings 57, 58 .

text.text: This is not a deficient version of European navigation but a different, internally structured frame that makes different operations cheap.

The historical parallel has five steps: an inherited frame stops supporting some operations; observers collect new relations; alternative coordinate systems are devised; their correspondences are calibrated against the same world; and navigators learn to act autonomously with the new frame.
The fifth step is decisive.
A map that works only while an expert points at it has not yet become the navigator's own coordinate system.

Neisser's Cognitive Psychology 59 helped establish a research language built on information processing, and Cognition and Reality 60 described cognition as a cycle in which schemata guide exploration, the environment modifies schemata, and changed schemata alter further exploration.

text.text: Reverse Cognition keeps the cycle and redirects the question: given an external certified structure and a learner with a particular repertoire, what sequence of representations can reorganize that repertoire?
The classical representational effect shows that formally equivalent tasks differ in difficulty across formats [61] [62] [63] .

text.text: The classical design runs forward: fix a problem, vary its representation, measure difficulty.

Reverse Cognition poses the inverse problem (Fig. 2): fix a certified structure beyond a given mind, search the space of representations for a route whose operations that mind can already perform, and test whether what is learned survives once the representation and the machine are withdrawn.

text.text: The inverse task is therefore not to generate many pictures but to build a path of partial, explicitly mapped representations along which a learner can carry an inference from one frame to another, and finally back to the symbolic object without support.
Mathematicians describe their own understanding in these terms 65 .

text.text: The proposal draws on, and must be distinguished from, several traditions.
Analogical transfer depends on mapping relational structure rather than surface features 66, 67 , and transfer is best measured as preparation for future learning 68 .

text.text: Machines enter this programme in four roles, and keeping them apart is what makes it testable (Fig. 3).
text.formatted: Machines enter this programme in four roles, and keeping them apart is what makes it testable (Fig. <ref type="figure" target="#fig_2">3</ref>).

text.text: As source, a machine supplies a structure whose correctness is fixed independently of any human: a Lean proof, a self-play concept, a validated model.
As generator, it proposes many candidate representations of that structure, far more than an instructor could design.
As auditor, it checks each correspondence between a representation and the certified structure, so that fidelity can be measured and manipulated rather than assumed.
As instrument, it records every step of a learner's navigation and estimates the learner's current repertoire, as knowledge-tracing systems do for skills 72 .
text.formatted: As instrument, it records every step of a learner's navigation and estimates the learner's current repertoire, as knowledge-tracing systems do for skills <ref type="bibr" target="#b71">72</ref> .

text.text: The fifth element is not a machine role but its absence.
The evidence that a mind has changed is gathered only after the machine and its representations have been withdrawn, after a delay, on tasks the learner has not seen.

Conditions that make learning feel easy often impair later retention, and difficulties introduced during learning can improve it 73 ; performance in the presence of the machine is therefore the wrong dependent variable.
text.formatted: Conditions that make learning feel easy often impair later retention, and difficulties introduced during learning can improve it <ref type="bibr" target="#b72">73</ref> ; performance in the presence of the machine is therefore the wrong dependent variable.

text.text: Results then flow back to the generator, which revises or rejects routes.
The loop is an empirical search over representations in which unaided human performance, not machine output, is the criterion.

Let K be a bounded mathematical target with proof obligations V and justified dependencies E. A representation r consists of a domain of claims D r , a specified mapping from representational features to mathematical objects, and declared operations.
A collection of representations forms a route when the learner can translate relevant objects and relations across them.
Each route carries a written scope statement: what it represents, which inference it licenses, and which conclusions it does not support.
We distinguish four audit dimensions (Table 1).
text.formatted: We distinguish four audit dimensions (Table <ref type="table" target="#tab_0">1</ref>).

text.text: Correctness: claimed correspondences are true in the stated domain.
Coverage: the route includes the claims needed for the learning target, not only an attractive fragment.
Inferential preservation: operations in one representation imply valid relations in the target.
Scope transparency: omissions, approximations and boundary conditions are explicit.
A wholly correct picture with minimal coverage is not a useful route.
"Certified" applies only where machine-checkable links have actually been provided; expert-reviewed analogies 66 are labelled differently.
text.formatted: "Certified" applies only where machine-checkable links have actually been provided; expert-reviewed analogies <ref type="bibr" target="#b65">66</ref> are labelled differently.

text.text: Accessibility is the estimated probability that a learner of specified preparation can perform the relevant inference under the stated representation and assistance.
Appropriation is a later change in unaided performance, especially on novel items and on counterfactual changes of assumptions.

For person i and target set T, let U i (T) be expected accuracy on pre-specified unaided inference tasks; a treatment effect is U i (T) delayed -U i (T) baseline relative to an exposurematched control.
Tasks, weighting, rater procedures and reliability must be specified in advance; this quantity is not a universal measure of understanding.
Whether routes can be built depends on the shape of the certified object, which can be measured.

Modularity and level lowering, which human mathematics attributes to different theorems and authors, reach 27,798 and 27,852 theorems respectively, 27,794 of them shared, although neither step cites the other.
What this sharing means mathematically requires expert interpretation.
For psychology, it is a concrete case of a machine organization of knowledge that does not follow the human conceptual partition, and it is the object a learner would have to navigate.
The formalization poses two problems at once.
Scale: about 13.5 million lines.
Time: at a rough 50 lines a minute, reading would take about 4,500 hours before any understanding began.
A Reverse Cognition system must compress both.
We propose that it do so with operations on the formal object that mirror known human cognitive processes, each testable with an established behavioural paradigm (Table 2).

Whether these translations change unaided performance more than the same content and time is the empirical question.
No human data have yet been collected.
The strongest competitor is not a naive "AI gives answers" account but ordinary generative learning from examples, diagrams, retrieval and feedback.
Studies must therefore match time, propositions, retrieval opportunities, feedback and visual material, varying only representational navigation.
If navigation improves only immediate confidence or practised items, expansion has not been shown.
If it improves delayed counterfactual performance and transfer beyond a well-matched active control, it gains support.
Certification and correctness must not be confounded.
An unverified explanation may still be correct, and a certified local identity may be irrelevant to the learning target.

One study should compare correspondence-audited with merely plausible material without knowingly teaching false propositions; a separate task can ask participants to identify clearly labelled invalid routes.
A "verified by AI" badge must itself be tested as an authority cue, and experts should audit materials blind to condition.

The promise and the risk follow from this distinction.
Reverse Cognition could give more researchers entry to unfamiliar structures; it could also concentrate influence if the generation and auditing of routes stay with a few organizations.

16 320 321 322 323 324 325 326 327 328 329 330 331 332 333 334 335 Conclusions The decisive change is not that an AI system outperforms people at a task, nor that its explanations are easier to read.

It is that we can now ask whether a certified external structure can become part of a person's independent inferential repertoire through a series of faithful, navigable transformations, and whether the age of machine knowledge will widen human understanding or contract it into dependence.
The southern sky offers a historically grounded model of such change: observation, comparison, new coordinates, cross-checking and acquired navigation.
The Fermat formalization offers a bounded, measurable test bed, not yet a psychological result.
Reverse Cognition will earn its place only if it predicts delayed autonomous inference beyond the effects of well-controlled ordinary learning.
